Article Title: IPL 2027: Amidst winds of change, Rohit Sharma is the glue Mumbai Indians need right now
Article Text:
Rohit Sharma and Kieron Pollard

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most important aspect for MI to focus on in the 2027 season? Restoring team chemistry Grooming future leaders Building a new strategy Retaining star players 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Kieron Pollard 's elevation as the new head coach and the exits of Mahela Jayawardene, Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson from the Mumbai Indians (MI) setup have already pressed the reset button in the camp. Appointments for the fielding coach and assistant coach are still pending, but the winds of change have well and truly arrived as the five-time Indian Premier League (IPL) winners look to return to their glory days.The biggest, and most crucial, piece in the puzzle, however, remains captaincy.Should they go back to Rohit Sharma ? The man who led them to five titles and understands the setup better than any other player? Or should they adopt a forward-looking approach with someone like Tilak Varma ? What about Jasprit Bumrah and Suryakumar Yadav?Rohit is 39 and isn't the best bet the franchise can make for the next cycle, but it's more about restoring normalcy, allowing Pollard to ease into his new role and possibly grooming the next leader in the final year of the ongoing cycle. After sweeping changes to the support staff, a sense of familiarity in the leadership group will only make the transition and preparation for future challenges smoother.Pollard and Rohit played together for several years at MI. The West Indian was part of the famous "engine room", also featuring Hardik and Krunal Pandya, that drove the franchise forward during their golden days and flourished when Rohit was at the helm.This is not to suggest that the two are the perfect recipe to restore order in that dressing room, but looking towards an inexperienced candidate at this stage will only complicate matters further. Tilak is taking giant strides in his cricketing career and is certainly the future leader of MI and Indian cricket. But right now, it's the delicate balancing act between need and want that could help the management find some answers.By no means should going back to Rohit come across as shutting the door on someone like Tilak. It's about keeping that door firmly secured until the stormy phase is well behind them and the management gains some sense of direction with the new personnel.The 2027 edition will be more about peaceful survival and getting things right as a group before the proper reset button is pressed ahead of the mega auction. Until then, even the biggest names in the setup, barring Hardik Pandya , whose potential trade is the talk of the town, will look to coexist. A sense of familiarity will help avoid the kind of drama that followed Pandya's high-profile trade in 2023.
Article Summary: Kieron Pollard has been appointed as the new head coach of Mumbai Indians. Mahela Jayawardene, Lasith Malinga, Paras Mhambrey and Carl Hopkinson have already left. The biggest, and most crucial, piece in the puzzle, however, remains captaincy.

Article Title: Nagaland United to add a new chapter to Talimeren Ao’s legacy by becoming first club from Nagaland on national stage with IFL debut
Article Text:
NUSC Stadium (left) and Talimeren Ao

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On the 107th anniversary of independent India’s first captain, Talimeren Ao, on Jan 28 last year, a new football stadium was inaugurated at the foothills of the Naga Hills in Chümoukedima, and a one-year-old club from the municipality played its first competitive match.Nagaland United FC lost that game 2-3 to Barak FC but wrote a new chapter in the football fate of the state that had given India the skipper who led the country from the front barefoot at the 1948 Olympics in London, carrying with him a nascent nation’s hopes in its first international campaign.And, on a chilly evening in Srinagar on Friday, Nagaland United will continue that legacy, albeit after a gap of 78 years, when they take on hosts Real Kashmir in the Indian Football League opener at TRC Stadium and become the first club to represent the northeastern state on the national stage.“Our aim in our debut IFL season is to build a competitive, disciplined, and fearless team that represents Nagaland with pride,” coach Kaizad Ambapardiwalla told TOI. “We want to compete strongly in every match, establish our identity through attacking football, high intensity, and teamwork, and challenge ourselves against the best teams in the league.”This promotion of a two-year-old club into the second-tier competition was courtesy of another club from the region that stamped its authority at the top tier by winning the I-League in 2017 – Aizawl FC.Having won their first tournament in October last year with the NSF Martyrs’ Memorial Trophy title, the club from Chümoukedima got the chance to face Aizawl FC on June 6, who came calling to their neighbours under the banner of Football for Peace and a “Match for Peace, Goal for Hope”.The visitors won that game 2-0, but three months later, on September 9, the All India Football Federation approved a goodwill agreement for Nagaland United to take a cash-strapped Aizawl’s place in the IFL, as the Mizoram club pledged technical and development support.Taking on the baton from a former I-League champion that has represented northeast for eleven straight seasons in the national league without relegation, Nagaland United will look to add another chapter in the football history of Nagaland, but of the football-loving northeast.“For me, it’s more than just playing at a higher level: it’s an opportunity to give back to the club that gave me my start, represent my state with pride, and hopefully inspire the young players back home to believe that their dreams, too, are possible,” 19-year-old Nagaland United defender Thejangulie Zatsu told TOI.“I know my journey is far from over, and I just want to keep growing, give everything I have for this badge, and make everyone who has believed in me proud.”On the evening of October 30, across Nagaland, people will gather around the screens: in community halls, in living rooms, in shops with their shutters half down as Nagaland FC get the opportunity to add another chapter to the story that started a hundred years ago with a Naga boy chasing a pomelo across a mission playground in the Naga Hills.“As a defender myself, his journey means even more to me because I play in the same position (as Amo). It gives me something to look up to and reminds me that where we come from should never limit how far we can dream,” added Zatsu.Friday will see that dream continue its journey from the foot of the Naga Hills to the Himalayan valley in Kashmir.
Article Summary: Nagaland United FC will play in the Indian Football League for the first time in 78 years on Friday. The two-year-old club will take on hosts Real Kashmir at TRC Stadium in Srinagar. Nagaland will become the first club from the northeastern state to represent India on the national stage.

Article Title: Who was Jilieta Gallego? Spanish long jumper among 69 killed in train collision
Article Text:
Cranes lift wrecked train carriages as rescuers search for victims following a collision between two trains in Urda, Spain.

Spanish long jumper Julieta Gallego, 24, was among those killed in a train collision in Toledo province that claimed at least 69 lives. The Royal Spanish Athletics Federation (RFEA) expressed its condolences following her death on Thursday."The Spanish athletics family joins in the grief over the passing of Julieta Gallego, athlete of AD Sprint, in the train accident that occurred in Urda (Toledo)," the federation said in a statement on X, offering its support to her family, friends and teammates at the club.Gallego represented Madrid-based AD Sprint and regularly competed in Spain's club championships. She recorded a personal best of 5.90 metres (19 feet 4 inches) in the long jump at Antequera in 2023."There are blows that strike at the very heart of the athletics family. Today, the sport mourns the passing of Julieta, a life ahead of her that has been unjustly extinguished," RFEA president Raul Chapado told Spanish newspaper ABC.Two high-speed trains collided on Wednesday in the second deadly accident in less than a year on the railway line connecting Madrid to the southern region of Andalusia.Former Spanish minister Fátima Báñez also died following Wednesday's collision.She served as minister for employment and social security between 2011 and 2018. Her death was confirmed by the Spanish Confederation of Business Organizations (CEOE), which she chairs.Rescue teams are continuing to search for survivors among the wreckage. The crash also left more than 100 people injured.A total of 544 people were travelling on the two trains when they collided between the towns of Mora and Orgaz, near Toledo. Several carriages derailed in the accident.
Article Summary: Spanish long jumper Julieta Gallego, 24, was among those killed in a train collision in Toledo province. The Royal Spanish Athletics Federation (RFEA) expressed its condolences following her death on Thursday.Gallego represented Madrid-based AD Sprint and regularly competed in Spain's club championships.

MYSORE: Former Karnataka skipper and star batter Manish Pandey , who hasn't featured in the state team since last season, has been named in the 34-member probables list for the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy T20 tournament. Article Title: Ranji Trophy: Tanush Kotian takes career-best 8-81 as Mumbai secure third bonus point win
Article Text:
Mumbai's Tanush Kotian raises the ball in the air as he greets spectators after taking a five-wicket haul with a total of 8 wickets in the second innings

Mumbai: Off-spinner Tanush Kotian produced a career-best 8-81 and an impressive match haul of 11-151 as Mumbai crushed Haryana by 10 wickets on the fourth and final day of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D clash at the MCA ground.The win gave Mumbai their third successive bonus-point victory of the season, marking their best start in a long time. They now have 21 points from three matches - the most among all teams in the Ranji Trophy - and sit atop their group, firmly placed on the road to the knockouts.Mumbai will next take on Railways at the Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India from November 2-5.The match will remain special for Kotian, who was playing his 50th first-class game. He marked the occasion with his first 10-wicket match haul and his fourth five-wicket haul.Chasing a modest target of 97, Mumbai openers Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Divyaansh Saxena completed the job in just 10.4 overs. Raghuvanshi, riding high after scoring his maiden first-class century in the first innings, smashed an unbeaten 67 off 39 balls. Saxena, who had struggled in his previous two innings, made a confidence-boosting 30 not out off 25 balls.The final day, however, was not entirely straightforward for Mumbai. Haryana's eighth-wicket pair of Samant Jakhar and Anuj Thakral made the hosts toil on a slow surface, adding 81 runs over nearly two hours.Kotian eventually broke the stand by bowling Jakhar. Haryana, who had resumed on 73-2, still 87 runs behind after following on, were bowled out for 256 in the second session.Reflecting on Mumbai's strong start to the season, Kotian said, "As a team, we've worked well. It's very difficult to get a third victory with a bonus point. Everyone is backing each other and giving confidence. We're trying to contribute together. If the team goal is going well, we want to keep moving forward like this."Brief scores: Mumbai 430 & 97-0 (Raghuvanshi 67*). Haryana 270 & (following-on) 256 (Kotian 8-81) Mumbai won by 10 wickets. Points: Mumbai 7, Haryana 0.
Article Summary: Mumbai beat Haryana by 10 wickets in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D clash. Off-spinner Tanush Kotian took a career-best 8-81 and an impressive match haul of 11-151. Mumbai openers Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Divyaansh Saxena completed the job in 10.4 overs.

Article Title: Asian Champions Trophy Hockey: India look to continue winning run against China
Article Text:
Image credit: Hockey India

Mandeep makes a strong statement

Fulton wants India to improve after the break

China present a different challenge

India will look to build on their strong start to the Asian Champions Trophy when they face China in their second round-robin match on Thursday. The five-time champions began their title defence with a big win over Bangladesh and will be keen to maintain their momentum against a young Chinese side.India, who recently won their second successive Asian Games gold medal to secure direct qualification for the Los Angeles Olympics, dominated Bangladesh in their opening match. Bangladesh replaced Pakistan in the tournament after the latter refused to travel to India, citing security reasons.The match was largely played in Bangladesh's half, with India controlling the contest. While Bangladesh were not expected to pose a major challenge, India's ability to score from both field play and penalty corners was an encouraging sign.The Harmanpreet Singh-led side scored eight field goals and five goals from set pieces against Bangladesh on Tuesday.Veteran forward Mandeep Singh was among the standout performers, scoring a hat-trick. His return to form comes at an important time, with national selectors expected to assess the players after the tournament.Mandeep was reportedly among four senior players who could be phased out after the ACT.The other three were Jarmanpreet Singh, Amit Rohidas and Nilakanta Sharma.Nilakanta announced on Tuesday that the tournament would be his last at the international level. However, Mandeep and Jarmanpreet are keen to continue playing.Apart from Mandeep's three goals, captain Harmanpreet, Dilpreet Singh and vice-captain Hardik Singh scored twice each. Shilanand Lakra, Nilakanta and Jugraj Singh also got on the scoresheet.India chief coach Craig Fulton was pleased with Mandeep's performance."He (Mandeep) was good, he did full of running and was nice and sharp, which was important," he said.Despite the convincing result, Fulton felt India needed to perform better in the third quarter, after the teams changed ends."We wanted a fast start, which we got in the first quarter. We wanted to play some fast-flowing hockey, which we did. But the third quarter wasn't that good, and that remains a problem. But I am glad we finished strongly," he pointed out.India had to manage without midfielder Manpreet Singh, who has been ruled out of the tournament because of a calf muscle injury. Hardik, Vivek Sagar Prasad and Nilakanta took charge of the midfield against Bangladesh and combined well with the forwards.Mandeep was a major threat in attack, with Abhishek, Dilpreet, Shilanand and Sukhjeet Singh supporting him.At the back, Harmanpreet, Amit Rohidas, Jugraj and Sanjay will continue to shoulder responsibility, while Suraj Karkera and Krishan Bahadur Pathak are the goalkeeping options.India will face a less familiar opponent in China, who pushed Asian Games silver medallists Malaysia hard before going down 4-5 in their opening match.China have brought an entirely new squad for the tournament, with their young players showing promise against Malaysia. Their lack of recent exposure against India, however, makes them a difficult team to assess.Fulton admitted that India had limited information about their opponents."This Chinese team is unknown to us, as they have come here with a completely new group, not the one that played at the Asian Games. We don't know much about them and haven't seen them play. We will have to analyse video footage of their match to get a fair idea about them," Fulton said.India will aim to carry their attacking form into Thursday's match while addressing the concerns raised by their coach. China, meanwhile, will look to build on their close contest against Malaysia and challenge the defending champions.Malaysia will face South Korea, while Japan will take on Bangladesh in the other matches scheduled for Thursday.Goalkeepers: Suraj Karkera, Krishan Bahadur PathakDefenders: Sanjay, Harmanpreet Singh (captain), Amit Rohidas, Jugraj Singh, Jarmanpreet Singh, Amandeep LakraMidfielders: Rajinder Singh, Aditya Arjun Lalage, Nilakanta Sharma, Hardik Singh, Vivek Sagar PrasadForwards: Shilanand Lakra, Abhishek, Sukhjeet Singh, Dilpreet Singh, Mandeep Singh
Article Summary: India will face China in their second round-robin match on Thursday. The five- time champions began their title defence with a big win over Bangladesh. Harmanpreet Singh-led side scored eight field goals and five goals from set pieces against Bangladesh.

Article Title: ISL: An attacking contest on card as leaders NEUFC lock horns with Bengaluru FC
Article Text:

KOLKATA: Still unbeaten after three matches, despite the frustrating stalemate away in their last game, NorthEast United FC will be back on Friday to continue their winning run at home and stay at the top of the Indian Super League table.“The mentality. We go into every game with the mentality that we are no longer the underdogs,” head coach Juan Pedro Benali said at the pre-match interaction on Thursday.However, on the other half of the field at Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium in Guwahati, will be a side that is also unbeaten in their ISL campaign and sit on the fourth spot having played one game less than the hosts.When NEUFC take on Bengaluru FC , it will be a test of the Highlanders’ defensive solidity – having conceded just one goal in three games – against the attacking prowess of the visitors, led by India striker Ryan Williams.NEUFC were held to a goalless draw by Odisha FC in their previous outing, with striker Alaaeddine Ajaraie missing a stoppage-time penalty, while Bengaluru registered a 2-0 win over Chennaiyin FC through goals from Williams and Mihailo Perovic.Benali believes that the challenge for NEUFC will be as much about breaking down Bengaluru’s structure as it will be about managing their attacking threats.“The details, concentration and crucial phases of the game will make the difference,” Benali added, underlining the fine margins that could decide the final scoreline.NorthEast United, meanwhile, will look to use their own attacking options and vary their approach to create openings. And, despite Ajaraie’s late penalty miss against Odisha FC in the last game, the Spanish coach kept his faith in the skills of their Moroccan talisman.“I prefer to win 4-3. I don’t want 0-0. I want to win. If there is a penalty tomorrow, Ajaraie will take it. There is no doubt about it,” Benali made it clear.Bengaluru coach Pep Munoz is also aware of the Ajaraie threat to their defence on the day.“They have an identity, some patterns that they like to create and a clear style of play,” Munoz said on Thursday, adding that his team is prepared to face either a back-four or a back-five defensive system.Going into the match after a break, Bengaluru will also hope to keep up their winning run as the fixture looks destined for an exciting contest of attack and defence for the fans.
Article Summary: NorthEast United FC take on Bengaluru FC in the Indian Super League on Friday. The Highlanders are unbeaten after three games and sit top of the table. Bengaluru are also unbeaten in their ISL campaign and sit in fourth place. NEUFC were held to a goalless draw by Odisha FC in their last game.

Article Title: 'Enjoying the game has to be the fundamental,' says Tvesa Malik after top-10 finish at India Open
Article Text:
Tvesa Malik (TOI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For Tvesa Malik, a strong performance at the Women’s Indian Open was as much about mastering her mind as it was about getting her golf right. The Indian golfer finished seventh at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, carding a four-round total of one-under 287 (71, 73, 71, 72) to emerge as one of three Indians in the top 10. With Vani Kapoor finishing second and Pranavi Urs sharing fourth place, the home contingent enjoyed an encouraging week at the event.“I think everyone can see it. I’ve always been really proud of how, despite how small the Women’s Golf Association of India (WGAI) started out and how few girls have been playing, so many have gone on to play in Europe and overseas. It’s not an easy standard,” said Tvesa.The progress, she added, has been building for years, with Aditi Ashok establishing herself internationally before Pranavi Urs and other Indian golfers delivered strong performances, including at the Asian Games. The recent Women’s Indian Open, she felt, was another encouraging sign of that development.The emergence of young talent has also caught her attention. Ojaswini Saraswat, who made the cut at the Women’s Indian Open at just 13, offered a glimpse of the potential among the next generation. For Tvesa, however, the key to nurturing young golfers is ensuring that the desire to play comes from within.“A lot of the time, it’s actually their parents who come and ask questions about how they should proceed.For me, it has always been about enjoying the game. That has to be the fundamental. If that is there, the sky is the limit,” she said.She added, “Parents have an important role in helping young players pursue their ambitions, but the goals must ultimately belong to the children themselves.”While younger players today have access to better information and are developing their games at an early age, Tvesa believes they must also learn to manage expectations. The competition is becoming younger and more intense, making it important to balance ambition with patience.Reflecting on Ojaswini’s achievement, she said, “You have to realize that you’re still so young and there’s so much time. Continue learning, ride that experience, and, at the same time, don’t set expectations so high that they become unrealistic.”Tvesa’s own performance at DLF was a reminder of the importance of that balance. The demanding course, known for punishing inaccurate shots and misplaced approaches, requires players to remain composed even when things do not go according to plan.While her ball-striking had been encouraging, she felt her mental approach made the bigger difference during the week.“This year, I felt a bit more accepting of the course. When you play there and you’re from there, the expectations are always high. It’s such a fine line between pushing yourself and almost holding yourself back,” she said.Tvesa, who is familiar with the DLF layout, explained that a single mistake can have a significant impact because of the course’s demanding nature. Accuracy off the tee and precise approach shots are crucial, while missing a green in the wrong place can make even saving par difficult.Her ability to accept those setbacks and move on was particularly encouraging. She recalled how her caddie praised her composure after the final round.“My caddie said the biggest thing was not actually what I had played, but the fact that I didn’t get upset. That impressed him the most,” she said.For Tvesa, patience was the key. Rather than allowing a mistake to affect the rest of her round, she reminded herself that more opportunities would come.That mental adjustment is also central to the challenge she is working to overcome in her professional career. Although she feels her technique has improved significantly, the results have not always reflected the quality of her game.Tvesa, who is married to fellow professional golfer Ajeetesh Sandhu, said, “Your technique is good enough when you’ve practiced and played for this long. Then you have to find the small things that give you an edge. Awareness is a big thing, understanding where I’m making mistakes and why, rather than just spending all my time working on technique,”.Beyond individual performance, Tvesa believes Indian women’s golf needs stronger institutional support to sustain its progress. Drawing on her experience competing on the Ladies European Tour, she pointed to systems in countries such as Sweden, Germany, and Australia, where players receive assistance with accommodation, coaching, physiotherapy, and training facilities.“It’s an expensive game to play, and support is necessary for everybody. Having a team around a player also provides mental reassurance when travel, fatigue, and changing conditions affect performance,” she said.
Article Summary: Tvesa Malik was one of three Indians in the top 10 at the Women's Indian Open. The Indian golfer finished seventh at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram. Vani Kapoor finished second and Pranavi Urs shared fourth place at the event.

Article Title: Mirabai Chanu pulls out of World Championships with back issue; Gyaneshwari Yadav finishes eighth
Article Text:
India's Mirabai Chanu (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Commonwealth Games silver medallist Gyaneshwari Yadav finished eighth in the women's 53kg category at the IWF World Championships on Thursday, while India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the event due to a back issue.Gyaneshwari, 23, from Chhattisgarh, recorded a combined lift of 198kg, with 88kg in the snatch and 110kg in the clean and jerk, to finish on top of Group C. Her total was also better than those achieved by several lifters from Groups A and B.The Asian Championship silver medallist could have improved on her personal best of 199kg and secured a higher overall finish had she converted two missed attempts, one in each section.Chanu, meanwhile, was forced to pull out before making her much-anticipated debut in the 53kg category. She had been assigned to Group B with an entry total of 200kg but withdrew after experiencing back pain.China's Zhang Haiqin claimed the gold medal with a total of 221kg (98kg+123kg). American Eleanor Ulrey took silver with 220kg (98kg+122kg), while North Korea's So Hyon Kim secured bronze with 214kg (91kg+123kg).The snatch competition also saw seven lifters register lifts of at least 90kg, a benchmark Chanu has been working towards for more than six years.At the World Championships, lifters are divided into groups based on their declared entry totals, which represent the combined weight they intend to lift in the snatch and clean and jerk. Group A features those with the highest entry totals, followed by Groups B, C and D.The World Championships is among six events in the first phase of the qualification system for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
Article Summary: Gyaneshwari Yadav finished eighth in the women's 53kg category at the IWF World Championships. India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu withdrew from the event due to a back issue. China's Zhang Haiqin claimed the gold medal with a total of 221kg.

India will have a 17-member contingent, featuring 11 women and six men, competing across 11 sports at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Senegal from October 31 to November 13.Table tennis player Syndrela Das, badminton talent Tanvi Patri and swimmer Dhinidhi Desinghu are among the country's leading medal prospects at the fourth edition of the Summer Youth Olympics, which will be staged in Africa for the first time.Das will take part in the women's singles table tennis competition, while Asian Under-17 badminton champion Patri will represent India in the women's singles event. Desinghu is entered in three swimming events: the women's 100m freestyle, 200m freestyle and 200m individual medley.India's participation will span athletics, archery, badminton, beach wrestling, boxing, equestrian, judo, swimming, table tennis, windsurfing and wushu. The 17-athlete squad will be the country's smallest contingent at a Summer Youth Olympic Games.The 2026 edition will be held across Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly over 15 days. Around 2,700 athletes are expected to compete in 25 sports for 153 medal events. Ten additional engagement sports will also be part of the programme, but will not offer medals.Dakar 2026 will mark the first time an Olympic sporting event is held on African soil.The Games were initially scheduled for 2022 but were postponed by four years due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The previous Summer Youth Olympics took place in Buenos Aires, Argentina, in 2018.India have collected 23 medals across the three previous editions, comprising three gold, 16 silver and four bronze. The inaugural Games were held in Singapore in 2010, followed by Nanjing in China in 2014 and Buenos Aires in 2018.Organised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), the Youth Olympic Games are designed for athletes primarily aged between 15 and 17. Alongside sporting competition, the event features educational and cultural programmes aimed at promoting Olympic values, participation and international understanding.The 2026 sports programme includes athletics, swimming, breaking, skateboarding, beach handball, beach wrestling, futsal, coastal rowing, Baseball5 and Wushu Taolu, among others. Baseball5 and Wushu Taolu will make their Youth Olympic Games debut. Ten engagement sports, including golf, karate and surfing, will be held without medal events.
Article Summary: India will have a 17-member contingent, featuring 11 women and six men, competing at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Glenn Phillips and Michael Bracewell powered New Zealand to a massive 259 for seven against India in the fourth T20I in Auckland on Friday, with the hosts using an aggressive approach to post the highest total by any team against India in the format.The previous highest total against India was England's 257 for three in Southampton earlier in 2026. West Indies had also scored 252 for four in Ranchi in the same year.New Zealand's attacking approach came as little surprise after India had set the tone with their batting in the third T20I, which they won to take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.Phillips scored 107 off 49 balls, while Bracewell made 65 off just 25 deliveries. The pair added 115 runs off 41 balls for the fifth wicket, keeping the Indian bowlers under pressure with their search for boundaries.Phillips also moved to the top of the list for the most runs scored by a batter in a T20I series against India.New Zealand lost Tim Seifert and Daryl Mitchell to pacer Mayank Yadav early in the innings but recovered through a 59-run partnership between Phillips and Finn Allen for the third wicket.Allen and Bevon Jacobs then departed in quick succession, briefly slowing New Zealand's progress. However, Phillips and Bracewell took charge and attacked the Indian bowlers.Phillips first went after Prince Yadav, hitting the pacer for a six and two fours. He was even more aggressive against Nitish Kumar Reddy, taking 32 runs off the 16th over with a sequence of four, six, six, six and six.Phillips reached his half-century in 31 balls and made the most of Reddy's pace. The final six of the over sailed over the sight screen after Phillips struck it straight down the ground.Bracewell was equally aggressive at the other end. He targeted left-arm spinner Axar Patel, hitting him for three fours and a six in one over to bring up his half-century in just 18 balls.Mayank was India's most effective bowler on the day, using deliveries in the mid-140s to trouble the New Zealand batters. However, Bracewell also used his pace against him, hitting two consecutive sixes with a flick and a scoop.Bracewell was eventually dismissed leg before wicket by Prince after reaching his half-century, but Phillips continued to lead the attack.The partnership took New Zealand from 112 for four in the 11th over to 227 for five in 17.2 overs.Phillips then brought up his third T20I century in just 46 balls, hitting a straight six off Arshdeep Singh. He scored his second fifty in only 15 deliveries.The right-hander was dismissed by Reddy soon after reaching the three-figure mark, but New Zealand had already done most of the damage. The hosts scored 85 runs in the final five overs to finish on 259 for seven.

Article Title: 'Some of the things hurt me': Zimbabwe captain slams players' 'complacency' after series loss as Afghanistan go from 5 for 4 to score 221

Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza was left disappointed with what he called "complacency" among some of his teammates after his side suffered a 19-run defeat to Afghanistan in the second T20I in Sharjah on Thursday. The loss also handed Afghanistan an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Raza said his biggest concern was the attitude of some players after Zimbabwe had reduced Afghanistan to 5 for 4 in the fourth over. He felt the team had taken the opposition lightly at that stage, assuming Afghanistan would struggle to post a big total."For me, before I go too much in detail [about the match] - and I will address that in the changing room - the toughest part to swallow was the complacency that I saw from some of the boys," Raza said after the match.The Zimbabwe captain was particularly unhappy that some players appeared to believe Afghanistan would manage only 130 or 140 runs after losing four wickets early. He said the team needed to stay focused and remember that a match is not over until the final ball."[At 5 for 4] some of the boys were probably calculating that it will be - 130, 140 max - at the end of 20 overs. Some of the things that I saw on the ground today certainly hurt me and I'll address that in the changing room because, listen, it can happen but I think that's where you have to be mentally very strong and say, 'no, the game is never over until it's over - we still have a job in hand and I'm going to be the guy who's going to get the job done'."Before I dissect the game with batting or bowling, I think that's something that I felt today out there in the middle and that's something that needs to be addressed, not to take this game for granted because it can bite back and today is a great example."Zimbabwe had also kept Afghanistan to 45 for 5 at the halfway stage of the innings. However, Azmatullah Omarzai 's 116 off 50 balls and Ijaz Ahmad Ahmadzai's 52 off 27 deliveries helped Afghanistan recover and post 221 for 7.Raza then led Zimbabwe's fightback with an unbeaten 106 off 56 balls, but his effort was not enough to prevent defeat. He said he had tried to keep his emotions under control while batting after being unhappy with the team's approach in the first innings."When you're chasing 222, for me the biggest thing was to try and stay in control of my emotions because the way we conducted ourselves in the first innings hurt me," Raza said. "So when we go out to bat, for me it was trying to win the game from any position. That has been our motto and in my head, I was just calculating how best can I go about my business and hopefully the other batters chip in so that we can win the game."Up until the last two overs [by when they needed 46 from 12], we were backing ourselves to win the game but yeah, I think we left ourselves too much."Raza also said he would address the issue with his teammates in the dressing room, making it clear that his message would be stronger than what he had said publicly.

MUMBAI: Competing neck and neck with Madhya Pradesh's off-spinner Saransh Jain Tanush Kotian is doing his best to stay in the race and in the radar of national selectors.On Thursday, the 28-year-old took a career-best eight for 81 in 34.3 overs in the second innings against Haryana. Having taken three for 70 in 30.5 overs in the first innings, Kotian finished with match figures of 11 for 151. His effort helped Mumbai register their third consecutive bonus-point win of the season, as they beat Haryana by 10 wickets at the MCA ground in BKC on the fourth and final day of their Ranji Trophy Elite Group D match.The match was a special one for Kotian as it was his 50th first-class appearance. He marked the occasion with his first 10-wicket haul in a match and his fourth five-wicket haul."I have had four years of progress and improvement in my bowling. I did a lot of tours, I was also with the India team. They all guided me a lot, like I was practising with (BCCI COE spin bowing coach) Sunil Joshi sir, Jatin (Paranjape) sir and Rajesh (Sanil) sir (childhood coach and mentor). A lot of people have guided me. I am trying to use that experience in my bowling," Kotian told reporters after the match.The off-spinner, who took three for 30 against Chandigarh in Mumbai's opening match of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season, said he had worked on his line and length, added new variations and tried different angles to trouble batters."I have improved a lot in line and length. I have brought in two-three variations which are helping me in deceiving and beating the batsman. I am trying to do that in every match and working on my accuracy as well. I have worked on different angles. Sometimes when I was bowling from over the wicket to the lefty, I was using angles and crease and it looked better as I was not allowing the batters to get set. It was helping me in creating pressure on the batsmen and doubts in their minds," he said.Explaining what worked for him against Haryana, Kotian said he focused on bowling in the right areas and asked for specific field placements to support his plans."I was looking to bowl in good areas and the field set-up that I needed, I was specifically asking for it and bowling accordingly. I was able to create opportunities and was in a good rhythm."Kotian also scored his 20th first-class half-century in Mumbai's first innings. He said he had been working on improving his batting while focusing on accuracy with the ball."I have worked on myself. In batting, I’m trying to contribute in the lower order and improve further but in bowling, I feel that I've worked a lot on my accuracy. I feel that's the key. I'm accurately bowling at the right place. I’m also talking to the ‘keeper as to how it is going and I am happy with that," he said.Kotian was also asked whether Saransh Jain's performances, including his 13 for 89 (7-40 & 6-49) against Bihar in the third round, had added to the competition for a place in the Indian team."No, it's not in my mind. Even though they selected Saran Jain, he's doing well. I'm doing well too. But my aim is to perform as well as I can in the Mumbai team, or whether it's Irani Cup or Duleep Trophy, wherever I go, in every match, I want to perform like that. In batting and bowling, the selectors will do their job and I want to do my job," he replied.Kotian is yet to make his Test debut for India, but he travelled with the team for the final two Tests of the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia. During the tour, he sought advice from India's bowling coach and former South Africa fast bowler Morne Morkel, as well as Australia's spin great Nathan Lyon."I worked with Morne Morkel. I also talked to Nathan Lyon who guided me. I was also with (Ravindra) Jadeja. (Like in Australia), the bounce is extra so how can I bowl more over-spin balls. Over there, Nathan Lyon guided me with the run-up and how to use the over-spin. Whatever I learnt there, I’m working on that and working with seam positions and variations so that is helping,” Kotian told reporters on Thursday.Asked whether he had made any technical changes to become more comfortable bowling around the wicket to right-handers, and whether he was thinking about a possible India call-up for the home Border-Gavaskar Trophy series in January-February 2027, Kotian said his focus was on improving his bowling across different angles.“As for the BGT, we’ll see. I’ve focused on being equally comfortable bowling ‘around the wicket’ and ‘over the wicket’ to both left-handers and right-handers. Since last year, I’ve worked on ensuring that no matter which angle the captain asks me to bowl from, I feel confident in executing it,” he said.Kotian bowled 65.3 overs across the two innings against Haryana, doing so in Mumbai's October heat and humidity. He said he had been waiting for an opportunity to bowl a long spell and wanted to give the captain confidence in his ability to do so."I was waiting for this opportunity. I was trying to bowl as much as I could. I think this is the first time that I've bowled this much in a match. I'm giving the captain the confidence that I can bowl this much and can get that many wickets as well. In the last four years, we were all getting wickets together and this time I got the opportunity. The ball was coming out from my hand well and I was getting the wickets from one end," the Vikhroli resident said.Of the eight wickets he took in the second innings, Kotian said he particularly enjoyed dismissing Haryana's well-set No. 8 batter Samant Jakhat, who scored 40. He bowled Jakhat to break an eighth-wicket partnership."There was a partnership for the eighth wicket, and to have got the ball through the bat and pad (for the breakthrough) was something crucial as the game opened up after that," he said.
Article Summary: Tanush Kotian took a career-best eight for 81 in 34.3 overs in the second innings against Haryana. His effort helped Mumbai register their third consecutive bonus-point win of the season. Kotian is competing with Madhya Pradesh's Saransh Jain for a place in the Indian team.

The series is settled. Now it's time for some fun. Team India, the Harlem Globetrotters of world cricket, have continued their march through New Zealand, arriving from humid home conditions just a day before the series began and making it 3-0 in style over the course of just a week, which teams would normally use to acclimatise to foreign conditions.After the stupendous feasts the batters enjoyed on the drop-in pitches in Christchurch and Wellington, the focus shifts to unique Eden Park in Auckland, a ground originally built with rugby in mind.The straight boundaries here are probably only a little longer than your backyard, while the longer square boundaries will test the power of India's hitmen. New Zealand's bowlers will need the motivation to bend their backs after watching India chase 199 in 13.2 overs on Tuesday.The Black Caps are already hampered by the absence of experienced pacers Matt Henry and Lockie Ferguson, both sidelined by injury, and the Indian batters should be licking their lips.Ravi Shastri said on air the other day that a question he gets asked often in New Zealand is: "Will that 15-year-old play?" But Eden Park is new for many of us, and we'll have to work out the right length once we understand the pitch," said Varma, who has been phenomenal with his finishing in the series.Paceman Mayank Yadav was left out of the last two games after returning figures of 1/49 in the first. Bhuvneshwar Kumar, on his return, has conceded 49, 50 and 40 runs in the three games he has played, taking one wicket.Mayank's burst of pace could come in handy. With the series already won, it would not be a bad time for the team management to look to the future.

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.

She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.
Article Summary: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3 as Pranav Soorma strikes gold again
Article Text:
Sumit Antil and Pranav Soorma (ANI/PTI Photo)

Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep

Pranav Soorma defends club throw crown

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep at the Asian Para Games. Pranav Soorma defends his title in the men's club throw F51 event. Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar complete all-Indian podium finish.

Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal (Pic credit: X)

Mona's record-breaking run in shooting

Nishad's golden double in athletics

NEW DELHI: Double gold medallists Mona Agarwal and Nishad Kumar will be India's flag-bearers at the closing ceremony of the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Saturday, following outstanding campaigns in shooting and para-athletics.Both athletes won two gold medals each at the continental event, with Mona producing a record-breaking performance in shooting and Nishad excelling in the high jump and long jump.Their selection as flag-bearers recognises their achievements as India prepare to bring the Games to a close.The 38-year-old Mona opened India's medal account in shooting by winning gold in the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games-record score of 250.0 points. Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
Article Text:
Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

NEW DELHI: Thulasimathi Murugesan produced a memorable triple-medal performance at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Friday, winning gold and two silver medals as India's para-badminton contingent enjoyed a productive day in Aichi-Nagoya.The 24-year-old Paris Paralympics silver medallist capped her campaign with gold in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 event, partnering Manasi Joshi to defeat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final. The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. She then teamed up with Nitesh Kumar in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, but the Indian combination went down 21-11, 19-21, 14-21 to Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.Nitesh, the Paris Paralympic champion, enjoyed a successful day of his own, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver with Thulasimathi.The 31-year-old defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles final."Last time I was close, I was leading 19-16 in the third set, and then I lost. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Making his Asian Para Games debut, Naveen completed the win in 36 minutes.Pramod had to settle for silver after winning gold in the 2018 and 2022 editions. India's Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan also claimed silver in the women's singles SH6 final after losing to China's Li Fengmei.India continued to collect medals across disciplines on Friday. Para shooter Mona Agarwal won her second gold of the Games in the women's 50m rifle 3 Positions SH1 final, setting a world record with 357.5 points. She finished 3.8 points ahead of China's Cuiping Zhang.In para archery, Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi won gold in the men's recurve doubles event. Sandeep claimed the men's 400m T64 title, while Haney won gold in the men's javelin throw F37/38 event.India also added silver medals through Nithya Sre Sumathy Sivan, Pooja Jatyan and Bhawna Choudhary in women's recurve doubles, Parmod Bijarnia in the men's 1500m T46 and Nimisha Suresh in the women's long jump T47. Jehan Madan and Shubham Wadhwa secured bronze in men's doubles para table tennis MD4.India's tally stood at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with the country fourth in the standings. The contingent is chasing its best-ever Asian Para Games haul of 108 medals, achieved at Hangzhou in 2023.

Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final. Nitesh Kumar wins gold in men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver. India's tally stands at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with country fourth in standings.

India's Thulasimathi Murugesan added another medal to her growing collection at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games, settling for silver in the women's singles SU5 badminton event after losing to China's Yang Qiuxia in the final on Friday. The 24-year-old, who won silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, went down 18-21, 11-21 against the Chinese shuttler at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium.However, Thulasimathi's campaign is far from over, with the Indian still in contention for two more gold medals in the mixed doubles and women's doubles events. The Indian had produced a fighting performance in the semi-finals, rallying from a game down to defeat compatriot and World No. 1 Manisha Ramdass 19-21, 21-15, 21-13 and book her place in the final.The silver medal adds to Thulasimathi's impressive record in para-badminton, following her breakthrough performance at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, where she finished runner-up in the women's singles SU5 category.Thulasimathi will have two more chances to finish her campaign on a high.She has partnered Nitesh Kumar to reach the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, where the Indian duo will face Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.The Indians booked their place in the final after overcoming China's Li Mingpan and Xiao Zuxian in a hard-fought 42-minute semi-final. Her silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics marked a major milestone in her career, while her performances at the Asian Para Games have further strengthened her standing on the international stage.She trains in Hyderabad under coaches Pullela Gopichand and Irfan Sait while pursuing a degree in veterinary science at Namakkal.
