Article Title: Indian Football League: Nagaland United open new chapter for football in the state
Article Text:
From first match to national league in two years

Talimeren Ao: The man who put Indian football on the Olympic stage

‘We do not have the time’

Local players remain a priority

Bringing national-league football home

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A new chapter in Nagaland football

Nagaland United Sports Club will begin a new chapter in Indian football when they take on Real Kashmir in the opening match of the 2026-27 Indian Football League (IFL) season on October 30. The match will be played at the TRC Stadium in Srinagar.The club will become the first team from Nagaland to compete in the national league. Founded in 2024 in Chümoukedima, Nagaland United have reached this level in just two years, giving a state with a rich football history its long-awaited place in the competition.The club’s journey is also linked to Dr. Talimeren Ao, who captained independent India’s football team at the 1948 Olympic Games. Nearly eight decades after Ao led the country at the Olympics, Nagaland United will carry the state’s football hopes onto the national stage.Nagaland United played their first competitive match on January 28, 2025, against Barak FC. The game was the opening fixture at a newly opened stadium in Chümoukedima. The date was special because it would have been Ao’s 107th birthday.The team lost the match 2-3 but soon made their presence felt in the Nagaland Super League.They finished second among seven teams in the league phase, conceding only nine goals in 12 matches, and ended the season in third place overall.Forward Nisede Peseyie scored a hat-trick against 27 United and won one of the league’s individual awards. Head coach Khogen Singh was named coach of the season.Nagaland United added their first major trophy in October 2025 when they won the NSF Martyrs’ Memorial Trophy in Kohima. They recorded wins by 7-0, 2-1 and 4-0 in the knockout rounds before beating Chedema Village Youth Organisation 3-1 in the final on October 18.Arap Konyak, Joel Haokip and Manton Konyak scored in the final. The club also won the player of the tournament, best goalkeeper and best defender awards, while Singh was once again named the best coach.The story of football in Nagaland goes back to Ao, whose early days in the game were far removed from the modern facilities available to players today.He began playing football on the mission playground at Impur in the Naga Hills. Children played barefoot, using balls made from rags, woven cane or even pomelos.Ao’s father, the first Reverend in the Naga Hills, died of typhoid before his son reached his late teens. He had wanted Ao to become a doctor and serve the Naga people.Ao fulfilled that wish by practising medicine, but he also went on to make history in football.On July 31, 1948, he captained India in the country’s first Olympic football match as an independent nation. India faced France at Cricklefield Stadium in Ilford, east London, and lost 1-2 after conceding a goal in the final minute. Eight Indian players played without boots.When asked about playing barefoot, Ao famously replied: “We play football in India, whereas you play bootball.”After returning to India, Ao continued his medical career and became Nagaland’s first Director of Health Services. His legacy remains important in a state where football is closely connected to community life.“Football in Nagaland is more than just a sport,” says coach Kivilu Kiba.Despite the state's love for football, no club from Nagaland had played in the national league before Nagaland United's entry. The club's leadership felt that waiting to move up through the lower divisions would take too long.“It would have taken us years,” says Abu Metha, a member of the club’s board, “and we do not have the time.”Nagaland United secured their place in the IFL through a goodwill agreement with Aizawl FC of Mizoram. Aizawl had made history in 2017 by becoming the first team from the Northeast to win the national league. They secured the title after drawing 1-1 with Shillong Lajong on the final day of the season.William Koso, the first coach from Nagaland to earn an AFC ‘A’ licence, was part of Aizawl’s coaching staff during that historic campaign.The connection between the clubs grew stronger in June 2026, when Aizawl visited Nagaland for a match under the Football for Peace initiative. The fixture, held in Chümoukedima on June 6, was called “Match for Peace, Goal for Hope”. Tickets cost Rs 20, and the proceeds went to an orphanage. Aizawl won the match 2-0.Aizawl owner Robert R. Royte later backed Nagaland’s efforts to gain representation in the national league.On September 9, the All India Football Federation approved a goodwill agreement that allowed Nagaland United to take Aizawl’s place in the IFL. Aizawl also agreed to provide technical and development support to the Nagaland club.Aizawl had spent 11 consecutive seasons in the national league without relegation. The club will now continue to play in the Mizoram Premier League.The fixture schedule has added another link between the two teams. Nagaland United will travel to Shillong on November 25, the city where Aizawl won their historic title, before visiting Aizawl on December 7.With their first IFL season approaching, Nagaland United have been working to build a team and support staff capable of handling the demands of national-level football.The club advertised for coaches and support staff and received hundreds of applications. Candidates applied from countries including Argentina, Spain and Brazil.Although Nagaland United have inherited a squad and staff with experience of the national league, developing local footballers remains a key goal.This was highlighted on October 17, when 20-year-old central midfielder Ghuqhe Chishi and Vinato Achumi were recognised after being selected to represent the club in the IFL. Both players have come through Nagaland’s under-20 teams.The club now faces a demanding season. Coordinator Gentleson Vashum said the team would play 20 league matches, with 10 at home and 10 away.Plans are also in place to install FIFA-approved artificial turf at Chümoukedima, which would help the club prepare for the demands of the competition.Nagaland United want to become a symbol of the state across India and beyond. More importantly, they hope their presence in the IFL will give local footballers a clearer path to the national level.“Whenever you enter any arena,” Metha says, “you enter to win.”K. Neibou Sekhose, president of the Nagaland Football Association, has called the club’s entry into the IFL a historic moment. He has also stressed that this is only the beginning of the state’s ambitions in football.Nagaland United will play their first home match in the IFL against Gokulam Kerala on November 14 in Chümoukedima. It is the same venue where they played their first competitive match in January 2025.Dempo are scheduled to visit later in November, while Mohammedan Sporting will arrive on December 19.The 2026-27 IFL season will return to a full home-and-away format, giving Nagaland United the chance to bring national-league football to their home state throughout the campaign.The league has also reported a sharp increase in television viewership, with last season’s audience four times that of the previous season.Nagaland United have appealed to Naga communities living across India, particularly students, to support the team during away matches. Their opening game in Srinagar will be the first opportunity for supporters living far from home to get behind the club.Nagaland United’s rise from a club founded in 2024 to a place in the national league has been quick. But their debut means more than simply competing for points and victories.For a state that produced India’s first Olympic football captain, the club offers a long-awaited chance to turn its passion for the game into a lasting presence in Indian football.When the IFL season begins on October 30, Nagaland United will take the field for their first national-league campaign. They will also carry forward the legacy of Talimeren Ao and aim to create new opportunities for the next generation of footballers from the Naga Hills.
Article Summary: Nagaland United Sports Club will take on Real Kashmir in the opening match of the 2026-27 Indian Football League (IFL) season on October 30. The club will become the first team from Nagaland to compete in the national league. Founded in 2024 in Chümoukedima, the club have reached this level in just two years.

Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo beats Lionel Messi to win inaugural BOAT award for 2008 Manchester United season
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo (AP/PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cristiano Ronaldo has been named the inaugural winner of the BOAT (Ballon d'Or of All Time) award, with fans voting his 2008 campaign at Manchester United as the greatest individual season in the history of football's most prestigious individual honour.Introduced by France Football, the award was designed to spark debate over which Ballon d'Or-winning campaign deserved to be considered the greatest of all time. Ronaldo came out on top after a fan-driven voting process, beating long-time rival Lionel Messi to the honour.Fans favoured Ronaldo's first Ballon d'Or-winning season in 2008 over Messi's remarkable 91-goal calendar year in 2012, a record that still stands.Unlike the traditional Ballon d'Or, where an international panel of prominent journalists determines the winner, the BOAT award allowed fans to cast their votes digitally. The voting list featured some of football's most celebrated names, including Johan Cruyff, Michel Platini, Marco van Basten, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Kevin Keegan and Franz Beckenbauer. Real Madrid legend Alfredo Di Stefano and Brazilian great Ronaldo Nazario were also among the nominees.The voting process required participants to pay one euro, with organisers offering an additional incentive by entering voters into a prize draw for two tickets to the 2027 Ballon d'Or ceremony.The initiative attracted considerable interest, with thousands participating in the contest. More than 5,000 individuals voted multiple times in an effort to help their preferred player or campaign finish on top.Ronaldo and Messi dominated the final rankings, occupying the first 12 positions between them. The run was broken at 13th place by Brazil's Ronaldo Nazario, whose 2002 Ballon d'Or-winning campaign was the next highest-ranked season outside the pair.Ronaldo's victory adds another chapter to his long-running rivalry with Messi, with fans now having delivered their verdict on which of their standout Ballon d'Or-winning campaigns deserves the ultimate recognition.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has been named the inaugural winner of the BOAT (Ballon d'Or of All Time) award. Article Title: Why China Suspended La Liga Broadcasts After Kylian Mbappé's 'Dictator' Remark About Mao Zedong: Full Controversy Explained
Article Text:
Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe (AP/PTI)

What did Mbappé say about Mao Zedong?

Why has China suspended La Liga broadcasts?

Three Chinese brands end partnerships with Mbappé

A wider pattern of commercial fallout in China

Kylian Mbappé has issued an apology after a video in which he appeared to describe China's founding leader Mao Zedong as a dictator triggered a backlash in China, costing the Real Madrid forward commercial partnerships and prompting Chinese state media to suspend broadcasts of Spanish football league matches featuring him.The controversy erupted after a clip of Mbappé discussing his favourite meme circulated on social media. His comments drew criticism from Chinese authorities, football officials and commercial partners, with demands for both the French footballer and his club, Real Madrid, to issue formal public apologies.In response, Mbappé acknowledged that his words had caused offence and expressed regret over the reaction in China.“My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,” he said in a statement on Tuesday.“I apologize to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry.”The controversy stems from a video in which Mbappé was asked to identify his favourite meme featuring himself.The French forward replied that it was “a video someone made of a guy ... I think he was a Chinese dictator”. The clip then showed an edited image placing Mbappé's face on the body of Mao Zedong, China's revolutionary leader and the founder of the People's Republic of China.Football fans on social media frequently use the term 'dictator' jokingly to describe Mbappé, who is often portrayed in memes as overshadowing his teammates and even the clubs he represents. Images depicting him as Mao and other authoritarian leaders have also circulated online.However, the reference to Mao proved particularly sensitive in China, where the former leader continues to be revered by many despite the controversial legacy of his rule.Mao led the Communist Party through its formative years and its victory over the Nationalist Party in the civil war, before establishing the People's Republic of China. His rule also included campaigns such as the Great Leap Forward, an industrialisation drive that contributed to a famine estimated to have killed around 30 million people.The combination of the dictator reference and the edited image prompted criticism in China, turning what appeared to be a joke about a football meme into a wider controversy.The fallout extended beyond Mbappé after Chinese authorities and state media demanded an apology from the player and Real Madrid.China Media Group announced that it had suspended broadcasts of matches in La Liga and other games featuring the French star. It also removed advertisements featuring him and called on Mbappé and Real Madrid to issue apologies.The China Football Association separately said it had “lodged a stern protest” with Real Madrid and demanded a “public and formal apology” from both the player and the club. It said it firmly opposed remarks that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people.The broadcast suspension puts La Liga's commercial relationship with China under pressure, given the country's importance as a market for the Spanish competition.La Liga responded by distancing itself from the comments, saying Mbappé had spoken in a personal capacity and did not represent the league.In a statement, it said it “deeply regrets the offense caused to Chinese fans by Mbappé's recent comments”.The league also announced plans to introduce a communication protocol for players and clubs, while working with stakeholders in China to prevent similar incidents in the future.La Liga president Javier Tebas later said on X that he had met China's ambassador to Spain, Yao Jing, to discuss the controversy and seek a resolution.Tebas reiterated the league's commitment to maintaining its partnerships with China, including its strategic agreement with the Chinese league through 2029 and its deals with China Media Group.“Our commitment is to keep working together so that an individual episode does not harm the important advances achieved nor affect the millions of Chinese fans who follow our competitions. China is and will continue to be a strategic partner for La Liga,” Tebas said.The backlash has also affected Mbappé's commercial interests in China, where his image has featured prominently in advertising campaigns, from subway stations to elevator displays.Beverage company Dongpeng, dairy giant Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground announced on Tuesday that they were ending their agreements with the footballer.The companies issued similarly worded statements opposing “any words and actions that hurt national sentiment”. Although they did not specify the precise reason for their decisions, their announcements followed the circulation of the video featuring Mbappé's comments about Mao.Mbappé has appeared in campaigns for products ranging from electrolyte drinks to milk and cheese. One Dongpeng advertisement featured him delivering a slogan in Chinese, while a Mengniu commercial showed him alongside Argentine football star Lionel Messi.Chinese social media platform RedNote also joined the criticism. It said its content partnership with Mbappé had ended on December 31, 2024, and announced that it would remove related promotional material. The platform expressed opposition to “any conduct that hurts national sentiment”.Mbappé's RedNote account was also banned from accepting new followers on Tuesday.On Weibo, hashtags relating to Dongpeng ending its partnership with the footballer and several brands cutting ties with him topped the trending list. Calls to boycott Mbappé also gained traction, with some users criticising his remarks and telling him not to visit China.The controversy is the latest example of the repercussions foreign public figures and organisations can face in China over remarks perceived as offensive to the country.In 2019, Chinese state television stopped broadcasting NBA games after Daryl Morey, then general manager of the Houston Rockets, tweeted in support of anti-government protesters in Hong Kong.The latest episode has similarly drawn in commercial partners, sports administrators and broadcasters, with La Liga attempting to contain the damage to its relationship with Chinese audiences.While Mbappé has apologised and the Spanish league has distanced itself from his comments, the incident has highlighted how a remark made in the context of an online football meme can escalate into a dispute with consequences for broadcasting and commercial partnerships.

The controversy erupted after a clip of Mbappe discussing his favourite meme circulated on social media. His comments drew criticism from Chinese authorities, football officials and commercial partners, with demands for both the French footballer and his club, Real Madrid, to issue public apologies.
